messages:
Jordan (support): flagged via ticket #ACME-512 — multiple EU users reporting high latency (600-1200ms) and occasional 500s for text-generation API. customer says started ~08:10 UTC. attaching logs.
Maya (oncall): thx, pinging infra. any recent deploys to routing?
Ron (infra): no deploys to routing control plane since 07:30. I see a surge in failed gRPC connects from edge-proxies to eu-cluster between 08:09-08:17. initial guess: transient capacity -> fallback to us-east.
Jordan (support): customer also reports auth errors for some requests: "401 invalid token scope". different subset of requests 401 vs 500.
Tess (eng-runtime): 401s could be KMS region mismatch if token introspection hit wrong control plane. can you paste a raw request/response (headers + request-id)?
Jordan (support): pasting sample:
```
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3d
x-region-preferred: eu-west-1
x-proxy-edge: edge-5.eu
status: 500
body: {"error":"model_timeout","latency_ms":1182}
```
another one:
```
x-request-id: r-0a1b2c3e
status: 401
body: {"error":"invalid_token_scope","region":"us-east-1"}
```
Sam (sre): looks like some requests claim x-region-preferred eu but downstream got routed to us-east and token introspection used us-east KMS, hence scope mismatch -> 401. can reproduce locally by forcing edge->us-east fallback.
ops-bot: [08:21 UTC] alert: routing-fallback-rate > 5% on eu region for service text-gen-prod
Maya (oncall): Ron, can you check geoip DB and our edge->cluster affinity table? maybe a stale entry.
Ron (infra): checking... geoip DB updated at 03:00 UTC. affinity table last changed 06:50. But I see a delta: an autoscaler job at 08:05 briefly removed eu-serving pool from healthy set (flapping) because healthchecks returned 503 for ~40s.
Tess (eng-runtime): hmm healthchecks 503 -> autoscaler marks pool unhealthy -> smart-routing policy kicks in and falls back to nearest compatible cluster (us-east in this case). However we expected fallback to eu-burst cluster in same region. why didn't it pick eu-burst?
Sam (sre): policy evaluation logs show a bug: when eu-serving set is empty, the selector prefers nearest region by latency metric. latency metric incorrectly reported us-east < eu-burst because of stale latency sample (from previous day) still in rolling-window.
Jordan (support): so root cause: transient healthcheck flap + stale latency samples -> incorrect fallback to us-east -> token/KMS region mismatch -> 401s + high latency for EU users. any billing implications? customer reported unexpected token usage spike.
Ron (infra): billing shows duplicate billing events for a small percent of requests that routed cross-region: because rate-limiter labeling used region tag from downstream cluster, some requests were double-counted when proxied through a second cluster. escalation to billing team in 2min.
Maya (oncall): immediate mitigation options?
Tess (eng-runtime): 1) force-routing: update routing-policy to prefer same-region burst pools when healthcheck fails for <60s (temporary override). 2) flush latency rolling-window for eu region so selector re-evaluates. 3) short-term: return 503 to clients for degraded window to avoid cross-region auth break. I'm for 1+2.
Sam (sre): I'll push a hotfix to routing config to prefer region-local burst. rolling-window flush is low-risk, pushing that now.
ops-bot: [08:36 UTC] deploy: routing-config-hotfix v2026.03.08-rc1 -> applied to control-plane nodes
Ron (infra): confirming edge-proxies now routing to eu-burst. sample request r-0a1b2c3f shows x-region-resolved: eu-west-1 and 200 in 140ms.
Jordan (support): told acme-sre we deployed a hotfix and are monitoring. they asked for repro steps — provided them sanitized request/response and said we'll follow up with timeline + postmortem.
acme-sre: thanks, can you confirm whether any requests were logged with PII or full customer payloads while routed cross-region?
Maya (oncall): short answer: no, payloads are encrypted end-to-end per contract. cross-region proxying didn't change storage policy. will verify audit logs.
Sam (sre): audit: no unauthorized storage writes. billing team flagged ~0.8% of requests for manual review due to double-counting tag; will reconcile credits.
Tess (eng-runtime): long-term fixes: a) ensure latency rolling-window has weight decay and immediate eviction on health events, b) change fallback selector to consider region affinity tags ahead of raw latency when region-local burst exists, c) add token-introspection region fallback logic to try multiple KMS endpoints before returning 401 when header indicates preferred-region.
Maya (oncall): agreed. also add an alert: fallback-rate spike + cross-region-auth-fail > threshold -> auto rollback of routing policy to safe-mode.
Jordan (support): drafting a message to ACME with timeline + credits note. will include repro steps and temporary mitigation (hotfix) and ETA for postmortem.
Ron (infra): putting collected logs + request-ids in the incident S3 bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1780123456/
ops-bot: [09:05 UTC] incident: severity -> P2, owner -> Maya (oncall), postmortem-due -> 2026-03-10
Maya (oncall): creating postmortem doc and will @eng-runtime & @sre for review. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Jordan (support): ACME updated: latency normalized for their reported users, 401s gone after 08:36. closing the escalation but keeping the incident thread open for postmortem notes.
Tess (eng-runtime): saving a small repro script to the repo (sanitized) with steps: set edge->eu-serving unhealthy, force fallback, verify token-introspect region, check counters. will link in postmortem.
Sam (sre): follow-ups: add regression test for routing selector logic, reconcile billing credits with finance, schedule kube-probe tuning review.
Maya (oncall): end of thread — will link postmortem here when ready.
